subject: Clarify IP indemnity carve-out: notice windows and recoverable costs
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: NovelAI Contracts <contracts@novelai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify IP indemnity carve-out: notice windows and recoverable costs

Hi Sarah / NovelAI contracts team —

Thanks again for moving quickly on the MSA redlines. A few items came up in our review specific to the IP indemnity carve-out and how it interacts with the limitation of liability:

- We want to confirm the exact scope of the carve-out we discussed — specifically whether parties intend the liability cap exclusion to cover: (a) indemnity payments for third-party IP claims (including royalties and settlements), (b) direct damages awarded by a court for IP infringement, and (c) related defense costs.

- Notice and mitigation timing: your counter seemed to require prompt notice but didn't specify a deadline. From our side we typically ask for notice "as soon as reasonably practicable" but also want an explicit window to preserve evidentiary defenses (we've proposed 15 business days in other deals). Can you confirm what NovelAI needs?

- Defense control vs. settlement: we need clarity on whether NovelAI will require the right to control defense and settlements (standard for indemnitors). If so, we ask for cooperation covenants and approval rights for any settlement that admits liability or imposes financial obligations on Redwood.

- Recoverable royalties: we want to include royalties as a recoverable remedy if a claim is sustained, but we expect those recoveries to be tied to documented royalties and not open-ended punitive recovery. Is NovelAI willing to limit royalties to amounts that are reasonably tied to the claim (e.g., past/expected license fees) and require a final adjudication or stipulated judgment before payment?

I've attached our latest redline (redlines_MSA_v3.pdf) with the proposed clause we think preserves the intent of an IP carve-out while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure.

Would appreciate a short note on the four bullets above — if it's easier, let's book 30 minutes early next week to align and then loop in legal counsel.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_MSA_v3.pdf (PDF, 142KB)

From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@novelai.com>

Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@novelai.com>, NovelAI Contracts <contracts@novelai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify IP indemnity carve-out: notice windows and recoverable costs

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers from our side (high-level):

1) Scope: NovelAI's position is that the liability cap exclusion should apply to (a) amounts we are obligated to pay to a third party in connection with an IP infringement claim (including royalties and settlements) and (b) reasonable defense costs. We are not asking for punitive or exemplary damages to be excluded. We would prefer the carve-out language to be broad enough to capture royalties so the indemnity is meaningful.

2) Notice: we need notice of a claim "within thirty (30) days" of becoming aware, but will accept a "prompt notice" fallback for extraordinary circumstances.

3) Defense & settlement: NovelAI typically requires the right to assume control of the defense, provided we: (i) notify promptly of our election, (ii) use counsel of reasonable experience, and (iii) keep Redwood reasonably informed. If NovelAI assumes defense, we ask to control settlement negotiations, provided any settlement does not impose non-monetary obligations on NovelAI without consent.

4) Royalties: we can accept language that ties royalty recovery to documented damages and, in the case of a settlement, to amounts actually paid in settlement. We would still prefer that the indemnity itself remain uncapped as to amounts awarded/paid in connection with IP claims.

I've attached our redline for the IP section (counter-proposal_redline.pdf). We can talk through tradeoffs on Monday or Tuesday; Tom and I are available Tue 11/30 at 2pm PT or Wed 12/1 at 11am PT.

Best,
Sarah Jensen
Director, Legal — NovelAI

Attachment: counter-proposal_redline.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Clarify IP indemnity carve-out: notice windows and recoverable costs

Alex / Lauren —

Thanks for forwarding Sarah's reply. High-level legal recommendation so we can respond with a unified commercial/legal position:

- We should accept an uncapped carve-out for IP indemnity payments tied to third-party claims (settlements and final judgments) but tighten operational protections:
  * Notice: require written notice "within fifteen (15) business days" of Redwood's receipt of a claim (with a "prompt notice" qualifier for force majeure). Shorter window preserves Redwood's ability to investigate and preserve defenses.
  * Defense: allow NovelAI to assume defense, but add clauses that (i) NovelAI must provide written notice of assumption within 14 days of receipt of notice, (ii) NovelAI must retain counsel reasonably acceptable to Redwood (standard reasonableness), and (iii) Redwood may participate at its own expense and request regular updates.
  * Settlement: require NovelAI to obtain Redwood's prior written consent for any settlement that (a) imposes an injunction or continuing obligation on Redwood, or (b) admits fault in a way that could harm Redwood's business. For pure monetary settlements, NovelAI can settle if it provides full notice and the settlement is limited to monetary payment to the claimant.
  * Royalties: limit recoverable royalties to documented amounts based on adjudication or documented settlement payments (no speculative future punitive royalties). If NovelAI insists on interim royalty payments, require escrow + final accounting on adjudication.

- Consequential damages carve-out: preserve the mutual exclusion for consequential/indirect damages except for IP indemnity carve-out as described above. Do not accept language that opens consequential damages broadly.

- Procedural costs: propose Redwood be responsible for reasonable out-of-pocket costs that are not part of indemnified defense (e.g., internal remediation unrelated to the defense) — avoid open-ended cost shifting.

Proposed insertion (suggested snippet to include in our counter):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), the liability cap set forth therein shall not apply to amounts payable by a Party under this Section Y (Intellectual Property Indemnity) with respect to a third-party claim that the indemnified Party's use of the indemnifying Party's Services infringes such third party's intellectual property rights; provided that (i) the indemnified Party provides written notice of such claim to the indemnifying Party within fifteen (15) business days after becoming aware of the claim, (ii) the indemnifying Party has the right to assume and exclusively control the defense and settlement of such claim, and (iii) any settlement that would impose non-monetary obligations on the indemnified Party or admit liability on behalf of the indemnified Party shall require the indemnified Party's prior written consent. Royalties recoverable under this Section shall be limited to amounts actually paid in resolution of the claim or as finally adjudicated by a court of competent jurisdiction."

If NovelAI pushes for a 30-day notice or full control without our consent over injunctive settlements, escalate to GC. Otherwise I recommend we propose the above language back to them and give flexibility on the 15 vs 30 day window if they insist but secure the other protections.

Marissa
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Alex
